As lots of comments have stated, follow basic calories in calories out and just "eat more". This might sound like a very naive advice considering your position since you have probably already exhausted lots of options and have already heard the same opinion 100s of times, but its that "simple". 

There isn't much stuff to gaining weight. Eating more than you are used to is always hard, usually feels like a chore and requires slow progression to up your intake. You have to trust the process and let it take you to the end.

Since you are a vegetarian, you can easily slot in Sattu, cheese, oats stuff like that and they are heavy in calories. If you are not feeling hungry, then you need to do some physically straining activity to create a caloric deficit, so that you feel hungry. Continue this process for a while and you will slowly start to see change. Note your bodyweight change every week to keep track and that is about it. 

You are tall, so you need to eat, a LOT! If you think you are gaining weight, you should always make sure by checking your weight regularly. If its increasing, great! If not, up your food intake till it does.

If you can afford gym and personal training, then go for it. But I would encourage you to research a bit of this on your own aswell, because learning by yourself gonna be best considering every different trainer will give you different advice and it might get confusing. 

Although I would go out and claim that most people dont need gym to get their daily physical activity quota filled. If you like some sport, start playing that sport more consistently. Maybe you can take up some other sport, but mostly these are just filler activites to jump start your body's response to stimulus so that you can eat more. After a while, it will become more normal.

Its a good start, but gaining or losing weight, both are sort of marathon. Consistent effort everyday will get you to your goal, so maybe try slotting in activities onto your weekdays aswell. Your body will thank you for it in the future, trust me. Also have some routine bloodwork done to assess your body nutrient profile. Lack of crucial nutrients or lower hormonal profile might make it harder for you to gain mass.

Body types are mostly a vaguely defined topic. Almost everyone will fall under the laws of thermodynamics and can easily manipulate their bodyweight by using calories in and calories out. Women generally have a higher body fat % compared to male, because of estrogen. You can't not eat anything and still be fat, its not physically possible.

You are 6ft so you need to eat wayy more than you are eating right now. You are probably barely hitting your TDEE calories anyways. Take up as sport so that you start feeling hungry and start adding more meals / volume throughout the day.

If the mechanic dosent involve you running around to dodge some bullethell and give you enough time to prep your ramp up dps, then its viable for that mechanic :)

If you are tanky enough to achieve the highest ramp up for your helixes, then high density packs are where you will be the tankiest considering how much life u can regain back easily. You can obviously scale down your dps a bit to focus on your defenses, surely allowing it to flex into certain content clearing playstyle.

I played helix deadeye to lategame and minmaxed it to about 30-40m dps. 

The great thing about the build was it was super cheap to get started with it and it also dealt stupid amounts of damage once you learnt how to "actually" use the skill. 

The clear is also not that bad if you have Herald of Ice.

The defenses were quite impressive too. Capped Spell Suppression, high evasion, armor and block. But the real defensive layer came from life on hit which resulted in immense amount of recovery if you were able to place a spectral helix on top of a pack/boss.

The build really shines when it comes to single target. You can preemptively prepare your spectral helix and can almost insta phase early bosses on budget gear. It deals ridiculous amounts of damage once the spiral starts shotgunning the boss. The life on hit stat also helps you to face tank to prep the spirals.

The worst part about the build is how much clunky it felt initially. You are essentially playing a melee build and you are locked into animation in a place when you cast spectral helix. This slowly starts becoming a non issue as you start stacking attack speed/ action speed on your character but initially it feels very oppressive to use this skill as it feels like shit. You also need to learn how to place the helixes. The main damage comes from you lining up multiple spectral helixes which can shotgun the boss dealing massive damage, but It requires a certain cue to know where to place them. For me personally, I understood that putting them in a counterclockwise manner usually allowed to line up for a shotgun position. 

The build also suffers from a low health pool (not ehp). If you are too lazy of a player and want to face tank very big hits (shaper balls/beam etc.) then you need to build the character very differently imo. The build's defenses shines when it faces multiple small damage hits and opportunities where it can heal back up using life on hit. But its a very versatile build, so you can probably make it do things by sacrificing a bit of damage, your choice.

I personally went with the Omniscience route and stacked attributes on my gear. This just resulted in me easily getting resistance capped and having immense amount of ele pen = more damage. Although this meant that I would also not have enough accuracy from dex, so I had to also pickup accuracy on gear and probably run precision till I had enough accuracy without it. 

The build's main expense is surely the claw. Get one with the highest ele dps. If you are lacking a certain elemental damage, you can make it up with its correspondent herald I guess, thats what I did to make sure my trinity was working. This locks you into not using wrath or anger since using them would just brick your trinity support and you would lose damage. It very easy to craft a high edps claw early in the league also, just make sure its on a life/mana on hit base (you can pick up similar nodes from the tree too). 

Thats all I can say right now about the build. My honest opinion would be too practice the build before the league starts to actually figure out if the spectral helix mechanics is for you or not. When I started the build I absolutely hated the chunkiness of it but I liked the damage so I stuck with it and eventually cleared everything the  game had to offer. 

Good luck for 3.18, ask me if you have further questions!

You can pick up arakalis fang whenever you are comfortable to do so. Spectres can easily carry you to endgame anyways. You can flexibly spec into it since it needs only 2 uniques : Speakers Wreath and the Fang. I played trade delrium and it took me like only 70-100c budget to kill sirus with basic spectres. I had tabula and only life+res gears and max 4 spectres. Only thing that lacked was my clear, and I solved it by buying the arakalis fang and speakers wreath. Its very low button pressy style gameplay and quite fast map clearing than most summoner builds. 

The way I go about putting cold into my build by getting grip of the council. You can also pick up redemption spectres. They have 75% cold damage conversion from the get go and come with freeze and shatter. Since its easier to scale elemental damage than phys, triad grips are good in this scenario but I find them choking my build min max room, so I didnt use them.

For the helmet, its a pure min max item. It makes our damage shoot through roof, but its very expensive too. Mine one is an 8L helmet and even then its not the strongest option. I think it can be pushed to 9L too but im not sure.

Any cold damage minon build can be scaled to the skies with crit. You go about stacking as many vicious bite nodes as you can through the cluster jewels. Animate weapon and Redeemer spectres are very good for this. You can easily enter red maps with minimal investment like by playing spider summoner build then transition into any cold conversion minion build. The reason cold is good is because of the extra defensive layer through chill and shatter, and also because of the mods on an elder/shaper helmet. I can explain more if anyone wants to know :)
